description: Extension pack of chatter, callers, sponsors, and arcs for WRFM. Drop these into wrfm_station.json under the matching top-level array (chatter / commercials / callers / station_ids) once you have generated TTS audio and pinned to IPFS — set asset.cid then.

schemaNotes.asset: cid is null until you fill it. JukeboxProvider routes clips with a non-null cid into the appropriate pool at startup; null-cid clips are silently skipped.
schemaNotes.script: text field is the spoken script with inline [SFX:], [MUSIC:], [ROOM:] cues preserved.
schemaNotes.sequence: Clips with conditions.sequence form a serialized arc — play in conditions.sequenceIndex order across nights.

script.text:
[SFX: INTERCOM-CHIME]
"Human Resources reminds you the kitchen sponge is communal property. Communal. Property. *(beat)* Carla. We know. We all know. The cameras point *at* the sink, Carla… I'm not even mad. I'm impressed."
[SFX: INTERCOM-CLICK off]

[SFX: PAPER-RUSTLE]
"Effective Monday, the phrase 'circle back' has been retired. Effective Tuesday, it has been reinstated. Effective Wednesday, HR is being retired. *(long beat)* Effective Thursday, none of this matters."
"HR memo. Subject line: 'Please.' That's the whole memo. Just… 'Please.' *(beat)* I've read it forty times, darling. I think they're begging."

[SFX: INTERCOM-CHIME]
"Human Resources wishes to clarify that the phrase 'open-door policy' refers to a metaphor. *(beat)* Whoever has been removing the actual doors — and we know it's a 'whoever,' singular, this is not a movement yet — please return them. Some of us have meetings. Some of us have *secrets.*"
"Reminder: the office plant has a name. Her name is Cheryl. Cheryl is doing her best. *(beat)* Cheryl is doing better than several of you."

[SFX: TYPEWRITER, three clicks scattered through]
"Tonight's Crime Blotter, second floor edition — 8:42 PM, theft of one yogurt, brand 'Noosa,' victim Carla, suspect at large. 9:13 PM, suspicious lanyard activity near the printer — perpetrator was holding two badges, neither of them his. 10:01 PM, unauthorized fish reheat. *(beat)* Kevin. *(long beat)* Always Kevin."

"Crime Blotter, after-midnight watch — at 1:14 AM, a desk plant was found relocated three cubicles east. The plant is fine. The plant is, in fact, thriving. *(beat)* We are now investigating whether the plant moved itself."

"This evening's Blotter — at 11:30, someone returned the conference room remote with all the buttons taped down. At 11:45, someone *un-taped* them. At 11:50, the buttons were *re-taped.* *(beat)* This is a war, sweethearts. We are watching."

"Crime Blotter — minor entry. At approximately 3 AM, the vending machine *gave* someone an extra bag of chips. *(beat)* Voluntarily. Without provocation. *(long beat)* This is not a crime. This is a miracle. We are filing it anyway."

---

[SFX: PHONE-RING, PHONE-PICKUP, loud mechanical keyboard under]
MITCH: "IT, Mitch speaking, have you tried turning it off and on again."
VERA: "Mitch. You called *me.*"
MITCH: "Right, well, the issue could be on your end."
VERA: "I am the radio, Mitch."
MITCH: "Have you tried turning the radio off and on again."
VERA: *(long beat)* "Mitch. I will."
MITCH: "Thank you for choosing IT."

MITCH: "Vera, just confirming — the password reset email I sent you, did you click the link."
VERA: "I did not."
MITCH: "Great. *(beat)* Don't."
VERA: "…Mitch."
MITCH: "I sent it from my personal account by accident. *(long beat)* Just — delete the whole inbox, to be safe."

[SFX: PHONE-RING, PHONE-PICKUP]
INTERN: *(small voice)* "Vera?"
VERA: "Sweetheart. Where are you."
INTERN: "I'm in the supply closet."
VERA: "Why."
INTERN: "I — I don't know how to print."
VERA: *(long beat)* "Buttercup, none of us know how to print. We have been pretending for thirty years."
INTERN: *(sniff)* "…really?"
VERA: "Welcome to the office, sweetheart."

[SFX: VERA-BUMP]
"Tonight's chatter is brought to you by ToneEase. *(SFX: spritz)* For when you need to say 'as per my last email' without sounding like you mean it. *(beat)* You mean it. ToneEase doesn't care."

"ToneEase Throat Spray. *(SFX: spritz)* Three pumps before the difficult conversation. Four pumps before the *very* difficult conversation. *(beat)* Five pumps and you are legally a different person, sweetheart. Use responsibly."

[SFX: spritz]
"ToneEase. The official spray of saying 'no problem!' through your teeth. *(long beat)* It is, in fact, a problem. ToneEase makes it sound like it isn't."

---
"There's a phone in this station, sweetheart. *(beat)* I'm not going to tell you where. *(long beat)* I don't have to. You'll find it. Most people do. *(beat)* Eventually."

"Did you know — and the station legal department asked me not to share this — there are *over a dozen* numbers that, if you dial them correctly, will get you somewhere you weren't supposed to be. *(beat)* Not all at once, darling. *(long beat)* Pace yourself."

"A friend of the station tells me that on a phone keypad, the letters V… E… R… A spell a number. *(beat)* I'm not going to tell you what number. *(long beat)* I assume, sweetheart, that you have fingers."

"Late-night advisory from the switchboard — there is, allegedly, a number that only connects between midnight and one AM. *(beat)* Don't ask me which one, darling. *(long beat)* I'm just saying. *(beat)* Some things are *time-sensitive.*"

"The station receives complaints, occasionally, that listeners have been dialing strange numbers and reaching strange voices. *(beat)* This is not a malfunction. *(long beat)* This is a *feature,* sweetheart. Try one. Any one. *(beat)* The phone is closer than you think."
